items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: And for some reason I was in Louisville and I went and spent the night talking to her and practically persuaded her to come back.

ctx.x: Well much was made of his innovative work with Louis Armstrong.

Well you see that actually worked against him. Because here’s a man who made his name really in 1928. He made “Weather Bird” with Louis and “West End Blues” which are two of the most famous records in jazz history. So people think, would automatically think of him as being old fashioned, because he was of the ‘20s. But he revolutionized piano playing, and he always asked people, other pianists, he said, “How do you do that?” And if they asked him how he did it, he would always show them.
